newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD, Bank of America buy into Polish Hortex.
newsitem.headline: EBRD, Bank of America buy into Polish Hortex.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and BankAmerica signed a deal with Polish food processor Hortex on Tuesday to buy a combined 41 percent of the firm for $28 million.
Hortex said in a statement that, under the agreement, the banks would increase their equity investment up to $53 million within the next two years.
The EBRD, BankAmerica and the current shareholders -- Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ), Bank Handlowy (BH) and others -- planned to list Hortex on the Warsaw bourse within the next three years.

"In addition to its fine growth prospects, Hortex is a unique vehicle through which to support the Polish fruit and vegetable farming community," the statement quoted Hans Jacobsen, director of EBRD's Agribusiness Team, as saying.

It said the EBRD and the BankAmerica will each hold 20.5 percent in Hortex, BGZ 25.5 percent, BH 13.2 percent and other shareholders, such as the WBK bank and farming cooperatives, will control the rest.

In the 12 months ending May 1997, Hortex posted sales of about 700 million zlotys and an operating profit of 45 million zlotys, compared with 561 and nine million zlotys in the similar period last year.
